cases.explain: «валаамова ослица» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: But Balaam’s ass had suddenly spoken. The subject was a strange one. Grigory had gone in the morning to make purchases, and had heard from the shopkeeper Lukyanov the story of a Russian soldier which had appeared in the newspaper of that day. This soldier had been taken prisoner in some remote part of Asia, and was threatened with an immediate agonizing death if he did not renounce Christianity and follow Islam. He refused to deny his faith, and was tortured, flayed alive, and died, praising and glorifying Christ. Grigory had related the story at table. Fyodor Pavlovitch always liked, over the dessert after dinner, to laugh and talk, if only with Grigory. This afternoon he was in a particularly good-humored and expansive mood. Sipping his brandy and listening to the story, he observed that they ought to make a saint of a soldier like that, and to take his skin to some monastery. “That would make the people flock, and bring the money in.” Grigory frowned, seeing that Fyodor Pavlovitch was by no means touched, but, as usual, was beginning to scoff. At that moment Smerdyakov, who was standing by the door, smiled. Smerdyakov often waited at table towards the end of dinner, and since Ivan’s arrival in our town he had done so every day.

cases.sentence: Григорий поморщился, видя, что Федор Павлович нисколько не умилился, а по ___ своей начинает кощунствовать.
cases.explain: «всегдашней привычке» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.

cases.sentence: Он с ___ обращался к Григорию, отвечая, в сущности, на одни лишь вопросы Федора Павловича и очень хорошо понимая это, но нарочно делая вид, что вопросы эти как будто задает ему Григорий.
cases.explain: «видимым удовольствием» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: He addressed Grigory with obvious satisfaction, though he was really answering Fyodor Pavlovitch’s questions, and was well aware of it, and intentionally pretending that Grigory had asked the questions.

cases.sentence: — крикнул вдруг Федор Павлович, — нагнись ко мне к ___.
cases.explain: «самому уху» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “Ivan,” cried Fyodor Pavlovitch suddenly, “stoop down for me to whisper. He’s got this all up for your benefit. He wants you to praise him. Praise him.”

cases.sentence: — Иван, опять ко мне к ___ нагнись.
cases.explain: «самому уху» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “Stay, Smerdyakov, be quiet a minute,” cried Fyodor Pavlovitch once more. “Ivan, your ear again.”

cases.explain: «чрезвычайным любопытством» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Yes.—But you’re rather drunk yourself,” thought Ivan, looking steadily at his father. He was watching Smerdyakov with great curiosity.

cases.sentence: Федор Павлович допил рюмку и залился ___.
cases.explain: «визгливым смехом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Grigory was thunderstruck and looked at the orator, his eyes nearly starting out of his head. Though he did not clearly understand what was said, he had caught something in this rigmarole, and stood, looking like a man who has just hit his head against a wall. Fyodor Pavlovitch emptied his glass and went off into his shrill laugh.

cases.sentence: Иван, заруби черту, запиши: весь ___ тут сказался!
cases.explain: «русский человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Stay!” cried Fyodor Pavlovitch, in a transport of delight. “So you do suppose there are two who can move mountains? Ivan, make a note of it, write it down. There you have the Russian all over!”

cases.explain: «русская вера» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “You agree. Then it must be so, if you agree. It’s true, isn’t it, Alyosha? That’s the Russian faith all over, isn’t it?”

cases.sentence: Да в этакую минуту не только что сумление может найти, но даже от страха и ___ решиться можно, так что и рассуждать-то будет совсем невозможно.
cases.explain: «самого рассудка» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Constitute a sin it may, but consider yourself, Grigory Vassilyevitch, that it only extenuates it, if it does constitute. If I had believed then in very truth, as I ought to have believed, then it really would have been sinful if I had not faced tortures for my faith, and had gone over to the pagan Mohammedan faith. But, of course, it wouldn’t have come to torture then, because I should only have had to say at that instant to the mountain, ‘Move and crush the tormentor,’ and it would have moved and at the very instant have crushed him like a black-beetle, and I should have walked away as though nothing had happened, praising and glorifying God. But, suppose at that very moment I had tried all that, and cried to that mountain, ‘Crush these tormentors,’ and it hadn’t crushed them, how could I have helped doubting, pray, at such a time, and at such a dread hour of mortal terror? And apart from that, I should know already that I could not attain to the fullness of the Kingdom of Heaven (for since the mountain had not moved at my word, they could not think very much of my faith up aloft, and there could be no very great reward awaiting me in the world to come). So why should I let them flay the skin off me as well, and to no good purpose? For, even though they had flayed my skin half off my back, even then the mountain would not have moved at my word or at my cry. And at such a moment not only doubt might come over one but one might lose one’s reason from fear, so that one would not be able to think at all. And, therefore, how should I be particularly to blame if not seeing my advantage or reward there or here, I should, at least, save my skin. And so trusting fully in the grace of the Lord I should cherish the hope that I might be altogether forgiven.”
